close_reason: Landed. TransportConfig::build_client now returns Result<HttpClient, ClientError>, not Result<reqwest::Client, _>. HttpClient is an opaque #[non_exhaustive] wrapper with pub fn new(reqwest::Client) for custom-impl construction and pub(crate) into_inner for internal unwrap. Debug renders as just 'HttpClient'. JmapClient::new and new_with_shared_auth unwrap at construction time. Two new tests pin the new return type (compile-time witness) and the custom-impl construction pattern. Partial-wrap rationale documented inline mirrors the ParseError/SerializeError pattern from JMAP-6r7c.26.
description:
auth.rs:38-41 — pub trait TransportConfig
  fn build_client(&self) -> Result<reqwest::Client, ClientError>;

The trait return type is `reqwest::Client`. This is the OPPOSITE of the SemVer-isolation policy applied to ClientError variants (which wrap reqwest::Error behind HttpError).

Implications:

1. **The transport CANNOT be swapped.** If this crate ever wanted to replace reqwest with hyper-util/ureq/curl, every consumer who has implemented their own TransportConfig (custom CA chain, custom client cert, etc.) would have their impl break. The trait commits the crate to reqwest forever (or to a major version bump).

2. **Asymmetric design.** Errors are wrapped (good); the constructor return type is not. The semver policy in the error.rs docstring (lines 5-13) says "reqwest and tokio-tungstenite are PRIVATE dependencies of this crate. Their types do not appear in any public function signature, variant payload, or `From` impl." That claim is FALSE for TransportConfig::build_client.

3. **An external impl is forced into the reqwest ecosystem.** A consumer who wants a custom transport (proxy support, custom DNS, etc.) must build a reqwest::Client. If reqwest doesn't expose the configuration they need, they're stuck — even though the JMAP client only uses .get() / .post() / .timeout() from the reqwest::Client.

Recommendation: wrap reqwest::Client in an opaque `HttpClient` type with the same SemVer policy as HttpError. The TransportConfig trait returns Result<HttpClient, ClientError>; the wrapper exposes only the methods this crate actually uses internally. Then reqwest becomes a true private dependency.

This is a known asymmetric leak and probably the right time to file it. The fix is a public API break (impls of TransportConfig change their return type), so it should ride the next major bump.
title: TransportConfig::build_client returns concrete reqwest::Client — leaks transport identity through public trait
